messages.subject: Re: Multiple session (Years) and trapping grids
messages.body_plain:
Hello Murray,

I really appreciate you taking the time to help. You were correct, there was no sampling effort in 2008, 2009 and 2015. I did as you suggested and removed the dummy row (and associated trap files).

The following code works and produces likely estimates on a linear link however does not account for missing years.

 secr.fit(SC_CH, model = D ~ Session, mask = mask)

When I attempt to include sessioncov and the model D~year (as below);

secr.fit(SC_CH, mask= mask, model = D ~ year, sessioncov = data.frame(year = 2006,2007,2010,2011,2012,2013,2014,2016)))

I get the following warnings:

1: In verify.capthist(capthist, report = 1) :
  Levels of factor covariate(s) differ between sessions
2: In FUN(X[[i]], ...) :
  bad densities in 'secr.loglikfn' (try different optimisation method, link, or model?

 I have attached the trace output from fitting the model. Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,
Michelle

On Thu, Mar 30, 2017 at 7:10 PM, Murray Efford <murray...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Michelle
> I'm not clear on the missing years: presumably there was no sampling effort in those years? If so then there was no relevant trap file and it is not appropriate to include a dummy row ('NONE') in the capture file*. I understand that you are concerned to allow for the spacing of sampling years when fitting the trend model; for that you should provide a session covariate (argument 'sessioncov', one row per session, in order). Something like this should work
> secr.fit(SC_CH, ..., sessioncov=data.frame(year = c(2006,2007,2010,2011,2012,2013,2015,2016)), model = D~year)
> Multiple year-specific masks can be provided as a list, one component per year. Better documentation is coming!
> Murray
>
> * I think your example might fail anyway because there were only 3 columns in those years.
>
>
> On Friday, March 31, 2017 at 12:15:01 PM UTC+13, Michelle McLellan wrote:
> > Hello Group,
> >
> > I am interested in estimating the change in density of a population (bears) over time using D~ Session where session is the year. I have multiple years of data where trap layout , the number of occasions and usage varies among years (extent doesn't change much). I have different trap files for each session(year) however I am uncertain how to deal with the trap files for the missing sessions(years). If I ignore them everything runs fine but I know this is not legit. I am also concerned how this will affect the later use of spatial masks.

> >

messages.subject: Pre-release secr 3.0 and new documentation
messages.body_plain:
Hello group
secr 3.0.0 is now in pre-release. It is available on the Density website <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/SECRinR.html> in virtually final form, and will be posted on CRAN in a few weeks. This is a major revision, and some changes in behaviour should be expected. Some estimates and likelihoods also change. There are big internal changes but most things should work as before. This is not true for telemetry and mark-resight data, which have changed significantly - see the much revised vignettes secr-telemetry.pdf <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-telemetry.pdf> and secr-markresight.pdf <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-markresight.pdf>. Polygon and transect data now require one of the hazard detection functions HHN, HEX, HHR, HAN, HCG. New documentation is provided as pdf files on the Density website: detailed accounts of habitat masks <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-habitatmasks.pdf> and multi-session data <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-multisession.pdf>, and an evolving introductory tutorial <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-tutorial.pdf>. Feedback that might improve these materials is most welcome.
Murray

messages.body_plain:
Hi Michelle
I haven't had that problem, but I can see how it might happen. With the default maximisation method there is a big step away from the starting values at about that iteration, and the slope coefficient went crazy, wildly inappropriate for a model for density on the log scale. I am surprised the algorithm didn't recover, as it usually does, so I'll look into that. The easiest fix is to try method = "Nelder-Mead" in secr.fit. I also guess that the original method might work with typsize = c(1, 0.01, 1, 1) included in the secr.fit call, or with link = list(D="identity"). I'm interested to hear how you go.
Murray

messages.subject: Detection functions in polygon detectors
messages.body_plain:
Using the updated detection function for polygon detectors, D for my study animal is now 4.2/100 km2. With the same parameters for the null model with detectionfn=HN earlier, density was 2.6/100 km2. So, if I had used results before the update, my density estimate would have been much smaller. But, just changing the detectionfn to HHN seems to increase D estimates. The same study would have yielded different densities.

Is this expected? Does anyone have a similar experience? I'm just wondering if I am missing something.

Thank you.
